commits.message:
[Performance][Model] Tile Qwen4Exp HC gate mix on Ascend A2/A3/A5 (#21901)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds an eight-row Triton tile for Qwen4Exp HyperConnection
`gate_mix`.
The existing one-row kernel remains the fallback. The row-block kernel
processes
an `8 x 512` tile, reduces the launched-program count by up to 8x, and
preserves
the original FP32 accumulation order.

The dispatch threshold is based on the integrated wrapper, not the
kernel alone:

- A2/A3: row-block starts at 2048 rows.
- A5: row-block starts at 1024 rows.

At 1024 rows the direct kernel is faster on all three devices, but
host-side
output allocation and custom-op dispatch dominate on A2/A3. A5 crosses
over
earlier and benefits from the row-block path at 1024 rows.

The shared `8 x 512` tile is close to the best measured per-device tile
at
1024 rows:

- A2: `8 x 512` is `80.00 us`; the best measured `4 x 512` variant is
  `78.86 us`, a 1.45% difference.
- A5: `8 x 512` is `14.63 us`; the best measured `32 x 128` variant is
  `14.57 us`, a 0.41% difference.

`512` divides the production `group_dim=2560` exactly, preserves column
alignment, and keeps one shared tile instead of adding per-device
tuning.
One hoisted mask is reused for all stream loads and the output store,
including
production-aligned and tail widths.

The implementation also handles column tails, combined row/column tails,
and
element offsets beyond `INT32_MAX`. The normal prefill path remains
int32.

No environment variable or user configuration is added.

### Operator integration

- Public wrapper: `hc_gate_mix(x, gate, hc_count)`
- Registered custom op: `qwen4_exp_ascend_hc_gate_mix`
- Production caller: `vllm_ascend/models/qwen4_exp/model.py`
- Validated model ABI: BF16 `[rows, 10240]` inputs, `hc_count=4`, BF16
output
  `[rows, 2560]`
- Operator guide:
  `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/qwen4_exp_hc_gate_mix.md`

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Large Qwen4Exp prefills can use the row-block operator path on A2,
A3, and
A5. Smaller prefills and unsupported profiles retain the existing
one-row path.
A release-note fragment is included.

### How was this patch tested?

Environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| CANN | 9.1.0 |
| Python | 3.11.10 |
| torch / torch-npu | 2.10.0+cpu / 2.10.0.post4 |
| triton-ascend | 3.6.0.post2 |
| EvalScope | 1.14.1 |

Functional validation:

| Check | A2 | A3 | A5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CPU dispatch/profile tests | 35 passed | 34 passed | 35 passed |
| Nightly Triton operator tests | 10 passed | 10 passed | 10 passed |
| Bitwise parity with legacy kernel | pass | pass | pass |
| NPUGraph replay | pass | pass | pass |
| Forced `WIDE_OFFSETS=True` parity | pass | pass | pass |
| Actual int32 boundary reference parity | pass | pass | pass |

The nightly suite now covers `group_dim=513` at rows 1024 and 1025, with
both
contiguous and row-strided inputs. These cases compare the row-block
kernel
against both the legacy kernel and the PyTorch reference, exercising
column
tails and combined row/column tails.

The int64 path has two levels of coverage. CPU tests check the exact
209,715/209,716-row host boundary and all three tensor strides. Separate
A2, A3,
and A5 runs each allocated 209,716 rows, selected `WIDE_OFFSETS=True`,
exceeded
`INT32_MAX` with `max_offset=2,147,491,839`, and matched PyTorch 64-bit
indexing
with `max_abs_error=0.0`.

The final PR does not modify `tests/manual/`. During kernel bring-up,
the
pre-existing manual script was used as a local NPU harness so boundary
and
replay cases could be run directly on the target board before nightly
integration existed. Once the coverage was formalized, refreshed-input
NPUGraph
replay moved to the nightly operator test and the temporary manual cases
were
removed. All deterministic coverage introduced by this PR now lives in
`tests/ut/` and `tests/e2e/nightly/`.

#### Real-serving compile reuse

A fresh-cache TP2 A3 serving probe hooked
`_hc_gate_mix_row_block_kernel._do_compile` in both real worker
processes:

| Phase | Input rows | Compilations |
|---|---:|---:|
| Startup | capture/warmup | 2 |
| Serving | 1024 | 0 |
| Serving | 2049 | 0 |
| Serving | 4096 | 0 |
| Serving | 8191 | 0 |
| Serving | 8192 | 0 |

The startup calls prepare the row-block variant once per worker.
Changing the
row count reuses it. The 1024-row request remains on the legacy kernel.

JIT specialization analysis:

- `rows` is annotated `do_not_specialize`, so changing only the row
count does
  not create another variant.
- `WIDE_OFFSETS` remains a compile-time constant for the rare
large-offset
  path.
- Exact-tile mask switches were removed. A3 measurements showed that
always
using the hoisted mask costs only 0.55% at 1024 rows and 0.04% at 8192
rows;
removing the switches avoids two constexpr keys, extra branches, and
separate
  compile variants.
- The real-serving probe observed one row-block variant per worker and
no
  unbounded row-count specialization.

#### Profiling follow-up

`msprof` was run on A3 with CANN 9.1.0, TP2 + EP, eager execution, and
four
`input=8192 / output=1` requests. The run completed `4/4` with
`failed=0`.
Profiling adds large collection overhead, so these numbers are used only
for
relative hotspot analysis, not as latency evidence.

The A3 trace was captured on one TP rank. The other rank did not produce
a
usable device trace. Its normalized NPU task-time distribution was:

| Kernel group | Share |
|---|---:|
| `_hc_combine_norm_kernel` | 12.86% |
| `ChunkGatedDeltaRuleFwd` | 8.97% |
| Grouped matmul path | 11.23% |
| `FusedInferAttentionScore` | 5.14% |
| AllToAllV AI CPU launch | 4.69% |
| `_hc_gate_mix_row_block_kernel` | 4.12% |
| Lightning Indexer + QSA mask preparation | 7.35% |

The optimized gate-mix kernel is no longer the dominant kernel-level
hotspot.
Further end-to-end work should focus on combine/norm, grouped matmul,
AllToAllV
launch overhead, and QSA index/mask preparation. Those items are outside
this
PR's operator scope.

#### 1024-row crossover

Medians use nine alternating rounds and 30 launches per sample.
Direct-kernel
timing uses preallocated output; wrapper timing includes allocation and
custom-op
dispatch.

| Device | Legacy direct | Row-block direct | Direct delta | Legacy
wrapper | Row-block wrapper | Wrapper delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A2 | 93.99 us | 81.71 us | -13.06% | 143.46 us | 173.85 us | +21.17% |
| A3 | 72.01 us | 45.88 us | -36.29% | 73.96 us | 88.11 us | +19.13% |
| A5 | 34.34 us | 14.47 us | -57.88% | 34.79 us | 18.18 us | -47.75% |

How to read this table:

- `direct` compares kernel execution only. The row-block kernel is
faster on
  every device because it launches fewer programs.
- `wrapper` compares the complete call path: output allocation, Python
validation, hardware-profile checks, custom-op dispatch, and Triton
launch.
On A2/A3 at 1024 rows, this host-bound overhead is larger than the
kernel
  time saved, so the complete row-block path is slower.
- The A2/A3 1024-row wrapper numbers are a forced experiment used to
select the
crossover. They are not the production configuration: both devices
retain
  the legacy path below 2048 rows.
- A5 crosses over earlier because its kernel saving is much larger, so
the
  complete row-block wrapper remains faster even after adding the common
  wrapper overhead.

Focused A3 decomposition at 1024 rows confirms the boundary:

| Path | Device time | Host enqueue |
|---|---:|---:|
| Output allocation only | 7.15 us | 6.25 us |
| Legacy direct | 73.05 us | 45.38 us |
| Row-block direct | 52.75 us | 50.83 us |
| Allocation + row-block direct | 64.87 us | 62.92 us |
| Row-block internal dispatch | 80.66 us | 77.56 us |
| Row-block `torch.ops` call | 90.58 us | 88.57 us |
| Row-block public wrapper | 94.52 us | 91.99 us |

The row-block kernel saves about 20 us, but allocation and host dispatch
add
more than that at this small row count. The family-specific thresholds
are
therefore part of the optimization, not evidence that the row-block
kernel is
slower.

`rows` with and without `do_not_specialize` differs by less than 1.3% in
these
direct measurements. The 1024-row behavior change is therefore caused by
the
integrated host crossover and dispatch threshold, not by the
specialization
annotation or kernel math.

#### A3 official end-to-end benchmark and accuracy

`vllm bench serve` configuration:

```text
random dataset, input=8192, output=1, 100 requests per arm
TP2 + EP, eager execution, max-num-batched-tokens=8192
fresh server and warmup for every arm
baseline -> candidate -> candidate -> baseline
```

| Concurrency | Throughput delta | Mean TTFT delta | P99 TTFT delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | +1.73% | -1.70% | -2.54% |
| 4 | +4.41% | -4.60% | -13.94% |
| 16 | +1.49% | -1.47% | -1.36% |

All reported performance arms completed `100/100` requests with
`failed=0`.

Full EvalScope GSM8K used all 1319 samples, greedy decoding, seed 42,
and
`max_tokens=512`:

| Run | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Run 1 | 92.57% | 91.21% | -1.36 pp |
| Run 2, reversed order | 91.58% | 91.36% | -0.22 pp |

Both runs completed `1319/1319` with zero errors. Model-level accuracy
varies
by about 1 pp across fresh server runs; the reversed-order run is nearly
equal.
The kernel itself is bitwise equal to the legacy implementation in the
tested
shape classes. No accuracy improvement is claimed.

### Merge status and scope

- A3 has full model-level performance and accuracy evidence.
- A2/A5 have full operator-level parity, tail, graph replay,
compilation, and
  timing evidence.
- Full A2/A5 model serving is not feasible with this checkpoint on the
available
hardware: the checkpoint is about 181 GB, while A2 has 32 GB HBM and A5
has
128 GB HBM. No A2/A5 model-level performance or accuracy claim is made.
- The Git merge state is `MERGEABLE`; GitHub reports `BLOCKED` because
required
  CODEOWNERS approvals are still missing.
- `DCO`, lint/static checks, CPU tests, nightly operator tests, and
local
  validation pass on the current local validation head.

[Feature] Support HiSparse with PCP decode request sharding (#21892)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable BF16 and native C8 HiSparse with prefill PCP and standard PCP
decode request sharding on Ascend 950 Model Runner V2.

- Use rank-local inputs for query and request-state handling, and
rank-major gathered rows for Resident cache and Host mirror writes. BF16
preprocessing sizes its workspace for all gathered rows and uses the
same write mapping as C8.
- Reuse Core's residency scheduling, DMA, completion fences and PCP
decode sharding policy. KV history is replicated across PCP ranks.
- Keep Target, draft prefill and later replicated draft decode layouts
aligned across graph capture and replay. The sharding changes from
#22069 are included.

Ascend-only change with no new operator or configuration switch. Base
HiSparse #20926 and Core PCP reuse #21846 are already in main.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. BF16 and native C8 HiSparse support PCP prefill and request-sharded
decode on Ascend 950 MRV2. Decode graphs and MTP are covered. Configure
eager Host mirroring and per-rank Host pools as described in the feature
guide. DCP, MultiConnector and external disaggregated P/D remain outside
the supported scope.

### How was this patch tested?

- Current BF16 functional runtime and test files match the on-device and
CPU-tested artifacts by SHA-256. Combined PCP CPU suite: 37 passed,
including BF16/FP16 write contracts, padded slots and PCP2/4 gathered
lengths. Prior C8 combined head `64dd8404`: 339 targeted CPU tests
passed.
- Ascend 950 PCP2, GLM5.3 with main KV and indexer BF16, TP4/EP8, MTP3
and decode graphs. Two-request graph smoke and completed 4- and
8-request waves. Forced BF16 Host-to-device recovery passed 6/6 device
checks. End-to-end BF16 was tested; FP16 coverage is CPU-only.
- The prior native C8 combined-stack validation completed all 16
requests at 32K input / 8K output on the same 18.8 GiB KV pool.
Whole-run output throughput was 460.97 → 583.65 tokens/s with HiSparse,
and preemptions decreased from 2 to 0. The input hashes matched; the
actual decode batches differed as the OFF run peaked at 11 running
requests. This is C8 capacity evidence for the previously tested
combined revision, not a BF16 performance result.
- For the BF16 functional patch, Ruff check, Ruff format and `git diff
--check` passed. Full repository CI has not been manually triggered.

This PR uses the existing unquantized SFA path. BF16 prefill performance
is addressed separately in #22371, which can merge independently.

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: empty local queries, padding,
sharded and replicated layouts, graph and draft transitions.

- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: CPU contracts, device recovery

[BugFix][Attention] Fix GLM DFlash2 FA3 HND caches and target graph warmup (#22159)

Current scope (`555017b3c`): GLM DFlash2 automatic FA3 selection
requires an eager draft (`speculative_config.enforce_eager=true`); the
target may still use graph execution. Early FA3 initialization and
resolved-layout binding are retained. The focused FA3 and DSpark
integration CPU contracts pass all 126 cases; full CI and hardware
validation remain required.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable the optional A2/A3 FA3 backend for eligible local GLM DFlash2
drafts while preserving the target attention backend and physical HND KV
storage. Prerequisite #20167 is merged; this PR contains the focused
follow-up.

- Preserve physical HND cache writes and expose the logical FA3 view
through a zero-copy transpose.
- Complete one-time generic FA3 native scheduler initialization in the
selected attention implementation constructor, **before model
profiling**. Retain inputs/results through synchronization and cache
successful initialization per worker/device/operator contract. The
constructor owns configuration/NPU availability eligibility;
initialization has no speculative-method or eager-only restriction. The
helper accepts an already-validated NPU device.
- Remove late initialization from the metadata builder and remove the
DFlash-specific target metadata filter. Keep draft attention groups, KV
allocation/binding, and connector initialization intact.
- Retain hardware, local PCP/DCP, dtype and fallback guards for backend
admission.

Controlled two-node A3 experiments found that first
`ComputeFAMetadataV3` CPU-function registration could remain pending
after profiling, including when initialized from the metadata builder.
Target warmup then waited in an all_reduce/NPUEvent synchronization
path. Initializing before profiling passed both with and without
metadata filtering; filtering is therefore not required to avoid the
observed hang in that configuration. The lower-level runtime/driver
mechanism remains unresolved.

The process-local initialization cache is written only after successful
synchronization. Forward and per-step metadata construction do not
update it or add these synchronization barriers. No pool policy, driver,
environment-variable or parallel-topology changes are included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Eligible local GLM DFlash2 drafts can use optional FA3 with HND KV
caches while the target retains its own attention and graph path. HND
layout resolution also honors the connector preference when no
environment override is set. Eager and graph draft configurations share
the admission/warmup logic; graph-draft hardware validation remains
pending.

### How was this patch tested?

Latest review update (`3d37ff50b`):
- **234 CPU contract tests passed** in the Ascend container, including
DFlash, DSpark, MTP and no-speculation configurations,
missing/unavailable NPU, constructor ordering, per-device deduplication,
and retry after failed initialization. CPU contracts explicitly disable
NPU availability.
- **8 A3 native FA3 cases passed eager and NPU graph capture/replay
against a CPU reference**: Q/KV heads 32/4 and 16/1, head dimension128,

[Performance][Model] Fuse the Step5 head-wise attention gate and indexer QKZ norm+RoPE kernels (#22401)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Following up on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20946.
Two model-specific Triton operator fusions for Step5-Preview on Ascend;
both replace eager chains that materialize intermediates and move
gate/indexer views across op boundaries (TensorMove on NPU):

1. **`gated_scale`** — fuses the post-attention head-wise gate (`attn *
sigmoid(gate)`) into one kernel, and (when `total_num_kv_heads >=
tp_size` and the packed shards are unquantized) packs the sliding-window
qkv and gate projections into one `qkvg` GEMM, so one matmul yields `[Q
| K | V | gate]` and the separate `g_proj` launch disappears. Callers:
`AscendStep5DSAAttention.forward`, `AscendStep5Attention.forward`.
2. **`indexer_qkz_norm_rope`** — fuses the DSA sparse-indexer chain
(per-head RMSNorm on `index_q`, LayerNorm on `index_k`, NeoX RoPE on
both, `index_z` passthrough) into one kernel, reading the strided
`split_indexer` views in place and storing `index_q` as e4m3, the dtype
the fused indexer scoring already consumes. Caller:
`AscendStep5DSAAttention._finish_indexer`.

Per gated layer per step this removes two eager kernels and one
materializing copy, plus one GEMM launch when qkv+gate packing is
active.

- Co-author for the indexer QKZ norm+RoPE operator optimization:
shengzhaotian <shengzhao_tian@163.com>.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

**Validation device:** Ascend 950DT only. Step5-Preview currently
targets 950DT; A2/A3 are not validated.

**Operator accuracy.** Single-operator e2e tests:
-
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_step5_gated_scale.py`
-
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_step5_indexer_qkz_norm_rope.py`
- 42 single-operator tests passed on Ascend 950DT.

**Model accuracy.** GPQA-Diamond accuracy evaluation:
- Evaluation Settings: `temperature=1`, `top_p=0.95`,
`top_k=0`,`max_tokens=1048576`

- Results

| Dataset | Accuracy |
|---|---:|
| GPQA-Diamond | **94.44%** (374/396) |

- Baseline Reference
Record **#20946** reported **GPQA 93.43 / MMMU_PRO 76.07** on the
double-node A5 DT pod.

**Performance.** End-to-end decode ITL at 64K input / 4K output:

| Batch | Baseline (both off) | `gated_scale` | `indexer_qkz_norm_rope`
|
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 36.977 ms | 36.404 ms (−1.55%) | 36.239 ms (−2.00%) |
| 32 | 39.312 ms | 38.747 ms (−1.44%) | 39.271 ms (−0.10%) | 

Conditions: Ascend 950DT, 2 nodes x 8 NPUs, DP4 x TP4 (EP16), MTP3, LLM
64K input / 4K output, streaming benchmark. The A/B disables each fusion
independently on the same code base. Prefill throughput stayed within
~2% across variants (24.1K-25.4K tokens/s). Single-run variance is about
±1%.

**Warmup.** No JIT warmup registration is used for these kernels;
required variants compile on first execution or during ACLGraph capture.
Geometry/capacity checks remain in the wrappers.

**Recompilation risk assessment.**
- *White-box*: `gated_scale` has constexpr head count/head_dim and no
autotune; runtime integers specialize only on Triton's `==1` / `%16` /
other classes, fixed per layer shape and anchor. `indexer_qkz_norm_rope`
autotunes once per (`head_dim`, `rotary_dim`) layer shape; token counts
are deliberately excluded, so prefill batch size changes do not retune.
Its runtime integers (`tokens`, strides) use the same bounded
specialization classes.
- *Black-box*: on Ascend 950DT, token counts 64 / 333 / 1024 / 4096 all
reuse one autotune key (`head_dim=256`, `rotary_dim=16`); no per-batch
retune was observed. `do_not_specialize` is not needed because the
specialization classes are few and fixed in serving.

[Feature][KV Pool] Enable prefill KV offload for GLM-5.3-Flash (#21256)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable prefill KV offload for GLM-5.3-Flash PD producers. AscendStore
uses Memcache to save and restore KV while layers rotate through a
shared NPU backing. Reuse waits for Store saves and outstanding PD reads
before overwriting a slot.

The GLM-5.3-Flash rules select main MLA and aligned KDA state for reuse.
Compressed indexer, tail, and MTP caches stay resident. Within each
block-stride bucket, the planner orders cache entries by layer, builds
packs with distinct cache groups, and assigns packs in slot rotation
order. A same-layer, same-group collision advances the search to the
next slot. The planner adds a slot when all existing slots conflict and
builds tensor descriptors directly from the slots. Core probes a
one-block layout to account for the backing. Independent layer IDs are
model-global.

With HBM prefix caching enabled, the scheduler keeps the existing local
block-hash lookup and counts external hits beyond the adopted local hit.
When a local hit includes rotating layers, the worker restores their KV
through AscendStore into the adopted block IDs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

GLM-5.3-Flash producers with text model type `glm5_next_text` can opt in
through `AscendStoreConnector` with `backend: memcache`, `use_layerwise:
true`, and `layerwise_num_shared_buffers`. In a `MultiConnector`
configuration, the planner reads the first AscendStore child. Leave
`layerwise_num_shared_buffers` unset for the Mooncake storage backend.
The planner recognizes the request without checking the backend, while
offload transfer requires the GVA data plane. Ordinary layerwise
pooling, models without registered reuse rules, and plans with no actual
rotation keep their native cache layouts.

[BugFix] Restore pre-fusion QSA preparation with current main ABI (#22633)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Roll back #22086's QSA preparation fusions on current vLLM Ascend main,
using the parent of its first commit
`151915c775f9eed9a060c87ceb7291d0b0034157`
(`03f69b977b088680686af6198cc52ab2a5bae542`) as the preparation
baseline. This is the compatibility-reviewed replacement for #22630;
only one rollback PR should be merged.

Restore the pre-PR preparation behavior:

- Gather clamped rotary cache rows outside the Indexer RMSNorm/MRoPE
kernel. The RMSNorm/MRoPE fusion that already existed before #22086
remains.
- Produce pooled compressed keys and their first positions, then
normalize, rotate and store them separately. Preserve compression before
raw-ring cache updates.
- Prepare native LightningIndexerV2 request lengths, query bounds and
FP32 score weights with the previous PyTorch operations. Keep V2,
request page tables, scheduling metadata reuse and the original
effective score weight.
- Inherit main QKV/Gate projection from upstream instead of using
#22086's Ascend projection override.

The five affected production modules have the same executable AST as the
pre-PR baseline, excluding docstrings; comments now describe the
restored behavior. Later main changes, including unrelated
operator-index additions, are retained.

### Compatibility with current main

Based on vLLM Ascend main `a285b50d4be519f0d4a713f01eb1d563592fbc3c` and
checked against its pinned vLLM commit
`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`.

The current packed-input ABI is retained: Indexer `attn`, `qkv`,
`slot_mapping` and `gate_out` arguments remain accepted, and its result
remains `(selected_indices, None)`. The Ascend attention owner still
materializes Q/K/V and the gate for packed inputs, updates the main
cache and dispatches attention through the current main interface.
Existing release-version dispatch is preserved.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next returns to its pre-#22086 preparation behavior,
removing the preparation speedups introduced by that PR. No
configuration change is required. No accuracy improvement or specific
runtime defect is claimed by this rollback.

### How was this patch tested?

- LightningIndexerV2 CPU contract and Qwen4Exp source guards: 14 passed,
with repository conftest excluded.
- QSA ABI tests: 9 passed in a dependency-isolated CPU audit using the
actual restored Ascend methods and the pinned upstream method
definitions. This includes new coverage for main's packed Indexer
arguments and external 1-axis/3-axis rotary-cache gathering.
- Audited executable AST equivalence of all five preparation modules
against `151915c7^` and verified main Indexer argument names, defaults
and keyword-only structure against the pinned upstream source.
- Ruff 0.14.0 lint/format, Markdownlint for the changed operator
documents/index, Python AST and whitespace checks passed.
- Full repository lint could not run locally because pre-commit is
unavailable. The isolated tests do not replace full vLLM/plugin imports
or hardware tests; NPU E2E, model accuracy and performance remain for
CI.

[Misc][KV Transfer] Log Mooncake heartbeat timing at initialization (#22643)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MooncakeConnectorV2 heartbeat logs do not expose the configured lease
timing, and timestamps alone cannot identify the heartbeat interval when
requests arrive intermittently.

Add one DEBUG `MooncakeHeartbeat event=config` per pull scheduler after
lease configuration validation. It includes the engine ID, KV role,
`initial_lease_s`, `renewal_window_s`, and `heartbeat_interval_s` (120,
80, and 20 seconds by default). The renewal window is measured from the
heartbeat processing time, not added to the old deadline.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

One initialization DEBUG record only. No configuration or runtime
behavior changes. No release-note fragment is included because
`release_notes/README.md` exempts internal logging changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- Passed Ruff lint, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` for the
final change, which adds only one logger call in `pull_scheduler.py`.
- Unit and NPU tests were not executed locally; runtime validation is CI
testing only. Updated the existing scheduler initialization test to
supply engine ID and KV role in its base-class mock, and assert exactly
one initialization DEBUG record with default (120/80/20 seconds) and
custom (60/40/10 seconds) values.

[BugFix] Fix KDA RecoverSSM small-norm accuracy (#22523)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #22413.

After the A3 fla_npu update in #22141, AscendC RecurrentKDA added `1e-6`
to the squared Q/K norm. RecoverSSM still normalized small nonzero
vectors to unit length, which caused four A3 Nightly verify-output
failures. The same mismatch could also change accepted-state
reconstruction.

Use `rsqrt(sum(x * x) + 1e-6)` in Triton verify, regular commit, and A5
grouped commit. Apply the same formula in the independent FP64
reference, document the formula, and restore the four regression cases
skipped by #22407. The constant is embedded in the FP32 arithmetic for
the existing kernels.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

RecoverSSM now matches native AscendC RecurrentKDA for near-zero Q/K
during KDA speculative decoding.

`flash-linear-attention-npu-a3==26.10.0+feature`. Reproduced the Nightly
failure at `405617bae` using image digest
`sha256:be1ff781b1d316c4f317c0b3925d2d1b6fc23c8993c30571ee5b5f5acd9e78c8`.

sources, all 6 amplitudes passed, including verify and accepted states

assert grouped dispatch and cover 32/64 heads with a six-token window in
eager and graph modes.

[Performance][KV Transfer] Reuse upstream hash truncation for Mooncake V2 (#22167)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

In Mooncake V2 P/D disaggregation, the producer removes the final prompt
token after block hashes have already been computed. The original
implementation clears all existing block hashes and rebuilds them for
the entire prompt before prefix-cache lookup, causing redundant hashing
of unchanged cached prefixes and increasing P-side scheduling overhead,
especially for long-context requests. This PR leverages the upstream
`Request.truncate_block_hashes()` API to preserve valid prefix hashes
and recompute only the affected suffix, avoiding unnecessary full-prompt
rehashing. In the previous NPU A/B benchmark (128K input / 1K output,
concurrency 32), this optimization improved output throughput by
**11.31%**, reduced mean P-side queue time by **18.1%**, and reduced
mean TTFT by **18.4%**. These performance results are from the original
implementation in #21857; no new NPU benchmark was performed for this
revision.

Related to #21437: its description explicitly proposes migrating
truncation sites to the upstream primitive to avoid full-prompt
rehashing. This PR implements that performance follow-up for the
**Mooncake V2 base scheduler**. #21437's hybrid/layerwise changes remain
a separate scope. The correctness rebuild was introduced by #20213; the
upstream primitive comes from [vLLM
#64096](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64096). This PR reuses
the upstream primitive and retains the original proposal's hardware
evidence below.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. With native hash-truncation support, long-context Mooncake V2
producer requests avoid hashing their unchanged cached prefix again
after the final prompt token is removed. Older cores keep the original
full-rebuild behavior. No new settings are required. A performance
release note is included in `release_notes/fragments/22167.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

CPU tests used independent checkouts of the Ascend and verified vLLM
commits above in the `pp-dspark` container. They execute real upstream
`Request` objects and the real truncation method, comparing the results
with an independent full rebuild.

```bash

OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -m pytest -q \
```

truncation method with token IDs/embeddings and lookahead 0/1/5; they
compare against full rebuilding and verify repeated-hook idempotency.
All 18 fail against the preceding unguarded implementation and pass with
the guard.

[Doc] Clarify release note rule for changes that cancel out before a release (#22660)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Clarifies that the unit of a release note is the **net change relative
to the previous release**, not the individual PR, and spells out two
recurring cases that current guidance does not cover:

1. **Bugfix cancelling an unreleased bug.** A fix for a bug that already
shipped in a released version needs a `bugfix` fragment. A fix for a bug
that never reached a released artifact (bug and fix both land between
two releases) needs no fragment of its own — instead the fix PR must
remove or amend the buggy PR's not-yet-archived fragment, otherwise the
release would announce a bug no released artifact ever contained.
2. **Reverting an unreleased PR.** A revert of a PR merged after the
last release has zero net change: no fragment, and the reverted PR's
not-yet-archived fragment is removed in the revert PR. Reverting
something that *did* ship is a user-visible behavior change and must
have a fragment (`breaking`, or `bugfix` if it reverts a regression).

Changes:
- `release_notes/README.md`: new section "Changes that cancel out before
a release"; explicit exception to the "fragments are archived, never
deleted" rule.
- `AGENTS.md`: one-paragraph summary in the Release Notes section,
linking to the README section.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Contributor-facing documentation only; no release note fragment
needed (this PR itself is the documentation change).

## How was this patch tested?

- Documentation-only change; no code affected.
- `markdownlint` passes on both modified files.

## Summary
vLLM's pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder` (#53558) is available on both
supported lanes now that the release lane tracks v0.33.0, so the monkey
patch no longer needs to carry Ascend's KV-cache planning decisions.

- `AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder` now owns grouping, pool accounting, and
materialization: it overrides `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` to
convert `num_blocks` through `_get_pool_bytes_per_block` and then
delegates to Ascend's planner.
- `patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py` is deleted entirely (640 -> 0
lines). Each of its two remaining patches had a concrete reason to go:
- **`_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups` duplicated the upstream
generic admission formula.** The generic planner derives admission from
two extension points: the builder `_get_pool_bytes_per_block` hook
(which already implements the kimi_k31 / turboquant / glm5next /
qwen4exp / DSV4 divisors) and spec-level `max_memory_usage_bytes` /

[CI] Explicitly disable static kernel for PIECEWISE SIT cases (#22631)

## Motivation

After #21921, `enable_static_kernel` is honored under the PIECEWISE and
FULL_AND_PIECEWISE cudagraph modes instead of being silently overridden
by `platform.py`. Static kernel compilation then runs per piece and per
cudagraph capture size at service startup.

The nightly cases touched here regress from tens of seconds of graph
capture to ~150-215 s **per capture-size step**, and are killed before
the accuracy stage:

| case | before (14:30 nightly, pre-#21921) | after (20:00 nightly,
post-#21921) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-A2 | 19 steps, ~43 s total | 150.85 s/step -> ~48 min,
hits `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` (1800 s) |
| qwen3-32b-int8 | 35 steps, ~26 s total | 214.76 s/step -> ~125 min,
hits the 2800 s `/health` timeout |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8_piecewise_fullgraph_A3 | 16 steps, ~52 s + ~41 s
| 98 s/step -> 26 min, then stuck on `FULL 0/16` |
| qwen3-32b-int8-prefix-cache | 35 steps, ~18 s total | 155.87 s/step ->
~91 min, hits the 2800 s `/health` timeout |

Evidence: both nightly rounds pin the same vLLM commit (`4ba787ec99`);
the only difference is vllm-ascend `6f60cb8fce` (pre-#21921) vs
`a38556f695` (post-#21921). The startup log shows `AscendCompiler hash
factors: {..., 'enable_npugraph_ex': False, 'enable_static_kernel':
False, 'enable_super_kernel': False}` before and all `True` after.
`running aisbench cmd` appears 0 times in all four failing jobs.

## What this PR does

Make the intended compile state explicit instead of relying on the old
silent force-off:

- `tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-A2.yaml` (2
server configs): `enable_static_kernel: false` **and**
`enable_npugraph_ex: false`
- `tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3-32B-Int8.yaml`:
`enable_static_kernel: false`
-
`tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Prefix-Cache-Qwen3-32B-Int8.yaml`:
`enable_static_kernel: false`
-
`tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8_piecewise_fullgraph_A3.yaml`
(2 test cases): `enable_static_kernel: false`
- `tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3-32B-Int8-A2.yaml`:
`enable_static_kernel: false` (same flag, same PIECEWISE startup path)

The other keys on those `additional-config` lines (`enable_flashcomm1`,
`weight_nz_mode`, `pa_shape_list`) are untouched.

`enable_super_kernel` is deliberately not written: `ascend_config.py`
makes it inherit `enable_static_kernel`, so it also becomes `False`.
Writing only `enable_static_kernel: true` was in practice enabling super
kernel as well.

### Why Qwen3-235B-A22B-A2 also turns `enable_npugraph_ex` off

#21921 removed a force-off that covered **all three** flags under
PIECEWISE, not just static/super:

```python
-        additional_config["ascend_compilation_config"]["enable_npugraph_ex"] = False
-        additional_config["ascend_compilation_config"]["enable_static_kernel"] = False
-        additional_config["ascend_compilation_config"]["enable_super_kernel"] = False
```

So this case's recorded perf baseline (`1152.0278`, `threshold: 0.97`)
was measured with npugraph_ex inactive. It is also the slowest of the
five to start even with everything off (~17 min of weight loading + FX
compile across 2 nodes, 2xDP x TP8, `--max-num-seqs 128` -> the largest
capture-bucket set), which leaves it the tightest margin against the
1800 s engine-ready timeout. Setting `enable_npugraph_ex: false` here
reproduces the pre-#21921 effective configuration exactly, so both
startup cost and measured performance stay on the baseline this case is
guarded against. The other four cases keep `enable_npugraph_ex: true`
(its default) to keep the FX optimization layer.

## Notes

- For the four cases that keep npugraph_ex on, this restores their
pre-#21921 startup behaviour while keeping the npugraph_ex FX
optimization layer active. It is a temporary mitigation to unblock
nightly; static kernel coverage for these models should be re-enabled
once compile artifacts can be cached/reused across runs (the static
kernel output directory is per-process today) or once the startup
timeout is raised together with a pre-warmed cache.
- Other case configs still enabling static kernel are out of scope of
this PR.
- No accuracy/perf gate semantics change: only the startup flags change;
the anomaly/accuracy gates are unaffected.

[BugFix] Fix DeepSeek V4.1 Engram post-load compatibility on Ascend (#22521)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Recent vLLM versions invoke `process_weights_after_loading()` on child
modules at the end of a load or reload. DeepSeek V4.1's Ascend Engram
embedding inherits a GPU peer-table finalizer that reads `peer_rows`,
which the Ascend constructor never creates. Startup fails with an
`AttributeError` after checkpoint loading.

Override the hook in `AscendParallelEngramEmbedding`. Ascend prepares
its own Engram storage during checkpoint loading, so there is no GPU
peer table to finalize. The regression test runs the vLLM finalizer on a
model containing an Ascend Engram embedding and verifies that the loaded
weight is preserved.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It fixes DeepSeek V4.1 startup with the verified vLLM main revision
when the Engram post-load hook runs.

runtime container.

containers. Both calls completed and preserved the weight parameter.
- The focused pytest regression passed in the Ascend runtime with CPU

[Feature] Opt-in layer-level BF16 MM ReduceScatter for SP (#21498)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Under sequence parallelism (SP), every attention O-projection on MiniMax
M3 is a TP-sharded GEMM immediately followed by a ReduceScatter. This PR
installs a layer-level `SequenceParallelMMReduceScatterOp` on those
projections so the GEMM and the ReduceScatter can execute as one fused
BF16 MM+ReduceScatter via `torch_npu.npu_mm_reduce_scatter_base`,
eliminating the standalone ReduceScatter kernel and its extra memory
traffic.

Why we need it: on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-bf16 (TP4+DP4+EP, decode-oriented
serving), the fusion delivers **1.16x–1.30x end-to-end throughput** and
**13–19% lower mean TTFT** across ISL 64–2048, with no regression
observed in the tested range (full data below).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. There is no API, configuration, or behavior change: the fusion is
opportunistic and only engages when SP is active and every gate passes;
otherwise the layer follows the stock path bit-for-bit. No release note
fragment is added.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests** (all passing, ruff clean; compatible with CPU-only CI
environments):

- `tests/ut/ops/test_mmrs.py` (new, 52 cases): every fusion gate (token
range [256, 16384), K range [256, 65535],
bias/LoRA/kv_consumer/PCP/existing custom op, weight
dtype/layout/format), numerical equivalence of the fallback path vs. MM
+ ReduceScatter, fresh weight view per forward, fused failure is not
silently retried as another collective, and hardware-capability gating.
- `tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_minimax_m3.py`: the op is installed
on attention O-projections only when SP is active, with the
model-supplied token limits.

`MM_REDUCE_SCATTER_BF16` capability.

**Performance benchmark: BF16 ISL sweep (OSL=1)**

- **Parallelism:** TP4 + DP4 + EP

`weight_nz_mode=1`, `max-model-len=2560`

[BugFix][DSV4] Load KV cache epilog before use (#22553)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix DeepSeek V4 FP8 KV-cache writes that reach `kv_compress_epilog`
before its CANN package has been imported. An empty-query PCP worker
still updates global KV, but can skip the query metadata path that
previously registered the operator.

Resolve the operator at its use site in `dsa_attn_kv_plan.py`: import
`cann_ops_transformer`, retrieve the operator, and cache the successful
lookup per process. KV writes then own their dependency independently of
query metadata. Package import and missing-operator errors propagate.
Existing dispatch, cache layout, slot mapping, and quantization
arguments are preserved.

The production change is confined to the KV writer. The failure analysis
and original fix came from
[li1how/vllm-ascend@07c8c40a](https://github.com/li1how/vllm-ascend/commit/07c8c40a5887f1a22edb4e1b6f6b6f433988eddc).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek V4 on Ascend A5 with FP8 KV caching can update global KV
from an empty-query PCP worker without depending on prior metadata
construction to register the operator. No configuration changes are
required. The installed CANN package must still provide
`kv_compress_epilog`.

### How was this patch tested?

- Reproduction: the first-use regression fails on the unpatched KV
writer with `AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'kv_compress_epilog'`.
- Fixed implementation: **9 CPU tests passed**:
  ```bash
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --confcutdir=tests/ut/attention
tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_kv_epilog_cpu.py
  ```
These tests execute the actual writer and loader functions with
dependency stubs, following the repository's isolated CPU-test pattern.
They cover first use without query metadata, cached reuse, import
failures, a missing operator after import, absent updates, and
non-epilog cache plans. They do not execute CANN kernels.
- Passed: Python syntax; the repository's Ruff, codespell, typos,
forbidden-import, and boolean-context-manager hooks; the direct
long-function check; and `git diff --check`.
- Full pre-commit remains pending: WSL Git 2.43 rejects the shared
repository's `relativeworktrees` extension. The native long-function

installed Python succeeds.
- **A5 real-NPU KV-writer regression passed** (CANN 9.2.1, torch 2.10.0,

metadata reproduced the original missing-operator `AttributeError`
before the fix. With the fix, first and repeated writes succeeded,
output bytes matched the original writer after explicit operator
registration, and unmapped cache rows remained unchanged. This isolated
check used real CANN/NPU tensors, not dependency stubs.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add Union sparse prefill attention for MiniMax-M3/M3.1 on Ascend A2, A3
and A5. Union merges up to eight adjacent queries within each request

The matching optional operators are [UnionSparseGen (ops-nn

Neither the hardware-profile module nor its tests are changed by this
PR.

[BugFix][KVPool] Request lazy store init for sparse-indexer models (#20538)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`KVPoolWorker` requests `lazy_init` from the storage backend only for
compressed models (`use_compress`, DSV4 `compress_ratios`) — the
deferral introduced for that family in #9771. Models that run the packed
C8 sparse-indexer KV pool path route their indexer KV through the pool
the same way but were never covered by that request, so the backend
always set the store up eagerly in its constructor.

The v0.26-based production chain shows what that ordering costs on
fabric memory (`ASCEND_ENABLE_USE_FABRIC_MEM=1`): with the packed C8
path active and the store set up eagerly at `KVPoolWorker` construction
— before the KV caches are registered — KV Pool startup hangs. Two
observations bracket the trigger:

- Turning the packed path off (eager setup unchanged) avoids the
failure.
- Deferring the store setup to the first `put()` — exactly what the
compressed path has done since #9771 — fixes it, with the packed path
itself untouched.

So the remedy is the store-setup ordering, but the failing surface is
the packed C8 path: eager setup plus a non-packed path does not
reproduce the hang. The gate therefore tracks the packed-path condition
rather than the model family alone. On main the v0.26 knob
(`c8_enable_reshape_optim`) no longer exists — the packed path is the
dtype-derived native default, active exactly when a sparse-indexer model
runs with an fp8/int8 `cache_dtype` (AscendConfig
`enable_sparse_sfa_c8`). The worker derives the same condition locally
from `vllm_config`, because the connector may be constructed before
AscendConfig is initialized:

```python
cache_dtype = vllm_config.cache_config.cache_dtype
packed_c8_path = self.use_sparse and cache_dtype in ("fp8", "int8")
backend_kwargs["lazy_init"] = self.use_compress or packed_c8_path
```

Blast radius is narrow: backends only honor `lazy_init` under fabric
memory (Mooncake) / `device_sdma` (Memcache), so other deployments see
no behavior change, and the lazy semantics (`exists()` reports misses
before init, `put()` triggers initialization) are unchanged since #9771.
Sparse models with other cache dtypes keep eager init — the trigger does
not reproduce there. `turboquant` stays out of the gate: it is a
different packed variant and was not part of the reproduced trigger.

A documentation section (motivation, semantics, and the affected model
families) has also been added to the Ascend Store KV Cache Pool guide,
as requested in review.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, a behavioral fix: for models on the packed C8 cache path (sparse +
fp8/int8 KV) on fabric-memory (Mooncake) or `device_sdma` (Memcache)
deployments, the KV Pool store is now initialized lazily on first use
instead of eagerly at startup, matching the compressed-model behavior
from #9771.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit test added in
`tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py`
(`TestLazyInitGate`): dense models request eager init; compressed models
request lazy init (#9771 unchanged); sparse + int8 and sparse + fp8
request lazy init (this fix); sparse + non-C8 dtype keeps eager init
(narrow-gate regression case). Full ascend_store UT suite: 999 passed,
12 skipped.
- Production chain on a v0.26-based deployment (GLM-5.x SFA + packed c8
indexer KV + Mooncake fabric-memory KV Pool): eager startup store setup
fails as described above; with the deferral the deployment starts and
pool operations initialize the store on first use.
- Doc section added to
`docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.md`
("Lazy Store Initialization"), covering why lazy init exists, the
first-`put()` semantics, and the affected model families.

[Refactor][MRV2][Attention] Refactor MLA Decode with UpdatableGraph (#21329)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Refactors MLA decode graph capture and replay in
`vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py` to use `UpdatableGraph`. The previous

from parallel parameter, handle, and event lists, so updates depended on

output tensors, removing the MLA-specific graph parameter bookkeeping.

layer's decode metadata. It pads target KV lengths, builds EAGLE target
query lengths, and supplies draft query lengths, KV lengths, and block
tables, including trimming the draft block table when padded batches are
disabled.
- Uses `get_capture_resource()` to allocate and reuse the FIA workspace
across captures. The speculative decoders are updated to pass MLA FIA
sequence-length and block-table parameters in the new form.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

[BugFix][Scheduler] Sync copied schedulers with upstream encoder input handling (#22206)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Balance (`patch_balance_schedule.py`), DyntraLB and Recompute
schedulers each keep a local copy of upstream `Scheduler.schedule()`, so
upstream fixes inside that method do not reach them. This PR syncs three
upstream changes into the copies and fixes one connector side effect
they expose.

- **vllm-project/vllm#59942** made `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` return
a fifth value (duplicate encoder inputs) and added
`_allocate_encoder_inputs`. The Balance and DyntraLB copies still
unpacked four values, so on vLLM 0.32 and later every multimodal request
raised `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 4)` and killed
EngineCore. Text-only requests never reach that line, which is why it
went unnoticed. The copies now take the fifth value and allocate through
the upstream helper, which also keeps the cache reference of a repeated
image. Recompute already followed upstream.
- **vllm-project/vllm#57368** lets the scheduler tell the Model Runner
V2 worker to drop a multimodal input's CPU payload once its placeholder
range is consumed, and to reinstall it when a rewind needs it again.
None of the copies, Recompute included, filled
`SchedulerOutput.encoder_input_updates`, so the worker kept every
request's pixels until the request finished. Each copy now forwards
`_get_encoder_input_updates()`.
- **vllm-project/vllm#41567** asks the EC connector
(`ensure_cache_available`) before each running chunk and before a
waiting request that resumes with computed tokens, not only for new
waiting requests. With `ECMooncakeConnector` that call is what starts a
load; `has_cache_item` also answers True for an item that is available
on the Encoder but not loaded. The Balance and DyntraLB copies only
checked new waiting requests, so an image whose encoder output was
evicted from the local cache between prefill chunks was scheduled as an
external load that no worker load served, and the model runner raised
`Encoder cache miss`. The two checks are added; Recompute already had
them. The connector hooks that change added to `update_from_output()`
and freeing are inherited unchanged.
- **`ECMemcacheConnector`**: with the running check above, the scheduler
asks the EC connector about every running multimodal request on every
step. `ECMemcacheConnector.ensure_cache_available` ignored
`num_computed_tokens` and forgets its hits each step, so each decode
step queried memcache again for inputs consumed long ago and counted
every answer as a hit. It now skips inputs whose placeholder range ends
before `num_computed_tokens`, as `ECMooncakeConnector` does. This
already happened with the default upstream scheduler, which has had the
running check since #41567.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Bug fixes only; see `release_notes/fragments/22206.yaml`. No new options
or default changes.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests** (CPU mode, vLLM v0.33.0): the 16 affected files under
`tests/ut/core`, `tests/ut/patch/platform` and `tests/ut/distributed`
pass (442 passed, 1 skipped; the skip also happens on main). New tests
in `tests/ut/core/test_scheduler_encoder_inputs.py` run against every
copied scheduler class:

- repeated-image cache references for waiting and running requests;
- CPU payload released after prefill and reinstalled after preemption;
- an evicted encoder output and a resumed waiting request, driven
through the real `AscendECMooncakeScheduler` consumer: the request is
deferred and a load is dispatched. With the Balance and DyntraLB checks
reverted, exactly those 6 cases fail; Balance then schedules the request
with no load dispatched for the image.

**End-to-end on Atlas A3** (Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, Balance with DP=2,
`--enforce-eager`, vLLM v0.33.0):

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #59942: one text and one image request through Balance | text OK;
image request returns HTTP 500, EngineCore dies with `too many values to
unpack (expected 4)` at `patch_balance_schedule.py` `schedule()` | both
OK, server alive; outputs match the default scheduler token for token |
| #57368: worker `update_encoder_inputs` traced | with the three
`encoder_input_updates` lines removed from Balance: no release | one
`{0: None}` per image request after prefill; under forced preemption
(2560-token KV cache, 8 concurrent image requests) the 2 preempted
requests are reinstalled and released again, all 8 complete |
| #41567: E + PD with `ECMooncakeConnector` (`mooncake_protocol:
ascend`, HCCS), Balance DP=2 on PD. Image B is warm in the PD cache,
request R = image A + ~4.5k tokens + image B is chunked 64 tokens per
step, and a request with 6 new images evicts B mid-prefill | with the
Balance checks reverted: PD raises `Encoder cache miss` for B and
EngineCore dies | R reloads B from the Encoder at computed=2816 and
answers correctly |

Not covered: DyntraLB and Recompute end to end (they run on
PD-disaggregated D nodes, which the EPD guide does not give an EC
connector; covered by the unit tests above), the streaming-input path of
the resumed-waiting check (unit test only), and the unit tests against
the pinned vLLM main commit (CI runs them).

Note: `/reset_encoder_cache` cannot be used to reproduce the #41567 case
on v0.33.0. That version does not reset the Mooncake connector on it and
crashes with `Encoder cache miss` with or without this PR; upstream
fixed that separately in vllm-project/vllm#66846.

[BugFix][Quantization] Recognize native packed MXFP4 checkpoints (#22426)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Native compressed-tensors checkpoints can contain static, symmetric FP4
weights in `mxfp4-pack-quantized` format, with group size 32 and
omitted/null activation quantization. Ascend rejects this recipe with
`No compressed-tensors compatible quantization type was found.` Add
recognition of the native weight-only recipe and dispatch it to the
existing `W4A8_MXFP` backend, which dynamically quantizes activations to
MXFP8.

**Known parsing limitation:** the existing `from_config()`
activation-format whitelist does not recognize top-level
`mxfp4-pack-quantized`. Explicit activation metadata can therefore be
discarded before scheme detection. This PR currently leaves that parser
behavior unchanged; the explicit-activation review concern remains
unresolved. The actual native Kimi K3 checkpoint has `input_activations:
null`, so it continues to select `W4A8_MXFP`.

**Companion vLLM dependency:** Kimi K3 also needs its vLLM model-config
hook to preserve compressed-tensors metadata on NPU. Restrict the
existing rewrite to CUDA/ROCm:

```python
from vllm.platforms import current_platform

if not current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
    return
```

This companion change belongs in vLLM and is not included here. With an
unmodified Kimi K3 hook, the earlier `mxfp4 quantization is currently
not supported in npu` error still occurs before Ascend scheme detection.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Native packed MXFP4 checkpoints without activation recipes can use
the existing Ascend W4A8 MXFP backend. No new CLI parameter or platform
patch module is introduced. ModelSlim code and kernels are unchanged.

`0.30.0rc2.dev304+geac9c0cf3` dependencies, with

[BugFix][Model] Skip unused DeepSeek V4.1 HC buffer for DSpark (#22485)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 currently uses `use_eagle()` to decide whether to allocate
the full HC hidden-state buffer. That predicate includes DSpark, even
though DSpark consumes the selected auxiliary hidden states through its
own storage. Serving with DSpark therefore reserves an unused
`[max_num_batched_tokens, hc_mult * hidden_size]` buffer and copies into
it on each target forward. With SP enabled, its presence also selects
the full-HC/pre-mix gather path.

Exclude DSpark at the V4.1 allocation condition. The existing
buffer-free forward path then handles collapse/gather, while MTP,
Eagle/Eagle3, DFlash and regular draft-model conditions remain
unchanged. No runner, shared `use_eagle()` semantics, or automatic-KV
accounting changes are included.

Target: `main`. Upstream vLLM uses the same exclusion in its [DeepSeek
buffer
predicate](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5173b1d5607ac9f0592e7600955fe8567f72e14b/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/spec_decode.py#L6-L16).
Related #16621 concerns DeepSeek V4 forward/runner operations; this
change fixes V4.1 allocation itself.

[BugFix] Handle padded graph rows in DSpark SWA indices (#22350)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix DSpark SWA indices when a captured graph keeps a fixed output row
count while the number of active token rows decreases.

- **PyTorch fallback:** for either caller-provided `buffer` or
`indices_output`, clone and pad the repeat counts to the fixed output
size, then mask inactive rows to indices `-1` and lengths `0` before
copying to stable output storage. This prevents the `repeat_interleave`
size mismatch.
- **Fused Triton path:** load `active_rows = query_start_loc[num_reqs]`
on device once per program and use it as the padding-cleanup lower
bound. Keep `num_rows` as the fixed output extent and buffer-check
value. The existing kernel clears padding in the same launch, without a
CPU synchronization or an additional mask operator. No constexpr keys or
specialization controls change.
- Add a regression that keeps six request slots and reuses the same
90-row index/length buffers for `[0,15,30,45,60,75,90]`,
`[0,15,30,30,30,30,30]`, then an all-zero batch. Every fused call uses
`num_decode_tokens=90`. Both direct launches and ACL graph
capture/replay check exact active rows, padding `-1/0`, fixed output
shapes, and buffer addresses.
- Update the operator documentation to distinguish the fixed output
extent from the device-side active row count.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Fix DSpark SWA metadata construction and stale padding when graph
replay has fewer active tokens than the fixed graph output size. No
configuration change is required.

[Performance] Compose fine-grained embedding & LM head TP with standard tensor parallelism (#19841)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fine-grained TP shards vocabulary weights along the **data-parallel
axis**. When stacked on standard `tensor_parallel_size > 1`, the
embedding and LM head knobs used to replace the standard TP sharding
with an equal-size fine-grained shard, so every TP rank kept a
replicated copy of its slice — a `tensor_parallel_size`-fold redundancy
in per-card weight memory and per-step weight reads.

Both knobs now **compose** with standard TP: the vocabulary is sharded
over the combined `finegrained_size × tensor_parallel_size` grid
(`shard_rank = tp_rank * finegrained_size + fg_rank`, the linearization
PCP_X_TP already uses), and one TP collective afterwards completes the
vocabulary result — an all-gather for the LM head, an all-reduce for the
embedding. The padding granularity is raised to `lcm(padding_size,
shard_count)`. With `tensor_parallel_size == 1` the behavior is
unchanged.

For example, with 8 ranks (`dp=4 × tp=2`, `lmhead_tp=4`):

| global rank | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **old** shard (`lhtp.rank`) | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| **new** shard (`tp.rank * 4 + lhtp.rank`) | 0 | 4 | 1 | 5 | 2 | 6 | 3
| 7 |

- Draft-model heads resolve through the same plan; the DFlash2 candidate
exchange appends the same TP all-gather so its Top-K union spans all
composed shards.
- `docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/Fine_grained_TP.md` documents
composing instead of replacing.

### Measured results (single-node stacked deployment)

Atlas 900 A3 (16 NPUs), MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-W8A8, DP4 × TP4 / EP16,
DSpark speculative decoding:

| config | before this PR | after this PR | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| fine-grained off | 34.55 GiB | 34.55 GiB | — |
| `lmhead_tensor_parallel_size: 4` | 34.55 GiB | 34.12 GiB | −0.43 GiB |
| `lmhead_tensor_parallel_size: 4` + `embedding_tensor_parallel_size: 4`
| 34.55 GiB | 33.69 GiB | −0.86 GiB |

Each vocabulary table is 2.29 GiB in bf16 (200064 × 6144) and the
deployment holds two per rank (`embed_tokens`, `lm_head`; the DSpark
draft reuses the target tables), matching the −0.86 GiB. Before this PR
a knob replaced the standard TP shard with an equal-size fine-grained
shard, so per-card weights matched the knob-off row. Enabling the knobs
costs a one-time ~0.47 GiB HCCL exchange-group allocation, constant
regardless of batch size, so the net KV-cache gain is +0.39 GiB per
card. Stacked e2e passes in both eager and cudagraph modes with
speculative decoding.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. In stacked deployments, per-card embedding/LM-head weight memory
and per-step weight reads drop by the tensor-parallel factor, at the
cost of one extra TP collective per exchange step. Numerics stay within
the standard vocabulary-parallel tolerance. Release note fragment:
`release_notes/fragments/19841.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests (`tests/ut/ops/test_vocab_parallel_embedding.py`): plan
resolution for both knobs (pure-DP vs composed), the composed LM-head
logits path, shard tiling across the composed grid, lcm padding, and the
embedding exchange lifecycle; plus the composed DFlash2 candidate Top-K
(`tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash_pcp.py`).
- NPU (Atlas A3): the touched files plus `test_lmhead_all_to_all.py` and
`test_ascend_config.py` — 180 passed, covering the `tensor_parallel_size
== 1` path.

[BugFix] Apply NZ mode to DeepSeek V4/V4.1 wo_a weights (#22165)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4/V4.1 unquantized grouped output projections skip NZ
conversion for `wo_a` even when the user selects `weight_nz_mode=2`.
This change removes the bypass and finalizes the grouped 3D layout
before applying the existing conversion policy, including for
dummy-loaded weights.

This ports the change from the operator integration branch
(pgzddxx/vllm-ascend#3) onto the current upstream `main`. It ports the
production fix and CPU regression coverage from #21652.

policy and quantized paths are unchanged.

weights**. The reusable receive buffers are allocated with

projections without a subsequent ND-to-NZ conversion. The setting can

[Feature][KV Transfer] Support KV-sharing layers in MooncakeConnectorV2 (#22157)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

A layer that reads another layer's KV cache declares
`kv_sharing_target_layer_name`. It owns no blocks, so it has no
`kv_cache_tensors` entry, but the model runner still registers it with
the connector, bound to its owner's cache. MooncakeConnectorV2 rejected
such a layer at registration:

```
ValueError: KV caches contain layers absent from kv_cache_tensors: [...]
```

So prefill and decode instances of models with cross-layer KV sharing
(for example Mistral Large 4) could not start with MooncakeConnectorV2.

`register_kv_caches` now validates these extra layers before registering
any memory. The implementation follows #22468.

- An extra layer is accepted only if it declares a target in the static
forward context, the target is a configured layer, and the layer is
bound to the same cache as its target (same device, address, dtype,
shape and stride for every tensor).
- Undeclared extra layers are still rejected with the original error.
Bindings to a different cache, missing owners and chained targets are
rejected.
- Accepted layers publish nothing of their own. Transfer metadata and
registered memory are identical to the owner-only case: the owner's
blocks are transferred once, and the sharing layer reads them through
its binding.
- KV sharing combined with KV parallelism (KVPP) is rejected with an
explicit error before KVPP rank mapping. Supporting that combination is
left for a follow-up.

The handshake format, scheduler, pull/push address calculation and
transfer-engine calls are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Models with cross-layer KV sharing can now start with
MooncakeConnectorV2 instead of failing at KV cache registration. KV
sharing with KVPP gives an explicit error. There are no new
configuration options. Release note:
`release_notes/fragments/22157.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests**, CPU only, with `torch_npu` mocked by
`tests/ut/conftest.py`:

`tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_base_worker.py`, each case run for
single-tensor and K/V-pair bindings:
- `test_register_kv_sharing_keeps_owner_metadata_and_registration`:
metadata and registered memory match the owner-only case, including
equivalent views and new K/V containers.
- `test_owner_descriptor_copy_is_visible_through_borrower`
- `test_register_kv_sharing_rejects_invalid_declarations`: undeclared,
missing, self and chained targets.
- `test_register_kv_sharing_rejects_different_bindings`: copy, other
owner, shape, stride, dtype, offset, count, empty.
- `test_register_kv_sharing_rejects_missing_owner`
- `test_register_kv_sharing_rejects_kvpp_before_mapping`

`tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_push_sending.py`:
- `test_shared_layer_hook_does_not_schedule_a_transfer`

`tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/test_kv_sharing.py`
runs the real pull path, with only the transfer engine replaced by one
that copies byte ranges:
- `test_pull_transfers_each_owner_once_and_borrowers_read_it`: each
owner block is read once, untouched blocks are unchanged, and each
sharing layer's binding reads the producer's owner KV.
- `test_pull_accepts_a_layer_that_only_the_consumer_shares`
- `test_pull_rejects_a_layer_that_only_the_producer_shares`

The valid-registration, KVPP, binding-check and pull tests fail against
`main`'s `base_worker.py` and pass with this change.

**Commands and results**, on Linux CPU with vLLM `c410543d`
(`.github/vllm-main-verified.commit`) installed with

```bash
pytest tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_base_worker.py \
```

[CI][BugFix] Tolerate a missing gate result artifact in the ci-gate comment bot (#22597)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

The `bot_ci_gate_comment` bot fires for every completed `CI Gate
Refresh` run with a `success` or `failure` conclusion. But a refresh run
that concludes **success without re-running anything** — comment-only or
non-owner review, already-green run, CI still in flight — ships no
`ci-gate-result` artifact (the artifact is only packaged when there is a
verdict to relay).

The bot's first download step then fails hard with `Artifact not found`
**before** the graceful `"no gate result artifact; skipping"` path in
the comment script can run, turning every such no-op into a red bot run.
Motivating example: run 44686050716, job 136120520568 (a successful
no-op refresh whose missing artifact reddened the bot).

Fix: add `continue-on-error: true` to the gate-result download step,
matching the `codeowner-details` step right below it, which already
needed the same tolerance. The comment script already handles the
missing artifact by skipping.

**This PR also switches the freshness stamp (merged in #22574) from UTC
to UTC+8** with an explicit `UTC+8` label, so maintainers read a
wall-clock time instead of doing mental conversion; a fixed offset is
used rather than the `Asia/Shanghai` tz database, which runners do not
guarantee.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. CI/dev tooling only: green no-op refresh runs no longer produce a
red `main CI Gate Comment` run on the Actions page.

## How was this patch tested?

- `bash format.sh ci` passes.
- CI testing only beyond that: the workflow only executes in the
repository context; the change is a single `continue-on-error` on an
existing download step whose skip path already exists in the script.

[Performance] Keep V4.1 Compressor batch extents dynamic (#21825)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Changing request count or allocated cache pages should not specialize
Compressor pooling/state-update kernels when layout and math stay the
same. Keep request/slot/page extents as runtime scalars and explicitly
disable scalar specialization for those arguments.

Head width, compression ratio, ring/chunk size, epsilon and
layout/algorithm flags remain constexpr. Projection autotuning is
unchanged. Pooling still precedes state update, and cache addressing is
widened to INT64 before multiplication. Public wrapper signatures and
A2/A3/A5 dispatch remain unchanged.

One functional commit contains the kernel change, release note and
operator contract. The operator document explains state mutation,
remaining specialization boundaries and reference/performance
validation. Private JIT cache hooks are not part of runtime behavior.

test-compatibility commit from #22471. The old unrelated shared CI/test
repair stack has been removed. The separate fixture change patches
legacy upstream PP getters only when they exist; DSpark handling and all

V4.1 Compressor avoids extra pooling/update kernel variants caused

[Feature] BigTensorLoader snapshot fast-restore via a shared weight-state kernel (#16734)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Two tightly-related pieces:

### 1. `--load-format bigtensorloader`: snapshot fast-restore

Restarting a vLLM Ascend instance re-parses safetensors, re-runs
`process_weights_after_loading` (quantization repacking, NZ layout
conversion,
MLA impl construction) and re-allocates final device buffers — a large,
repetitive cost for every restart of the same model.

This loader caches **each rank's final post-process device weights**
(one blob
file + one JSON manifest) after the first fresh load, and on subsequent
starts
restores them via mmap + batched H2D, skipping
parsing/repacking/conversion
entirely. Measured on Ascend 910B: **2x–7.7x faster `load_model`**
across dense
bf16, W8A8-quantized, multimodal and MoE+MLA models, with byte-identical
serving outputs.

Correctness-first design:

- **Container capture**: list/dict-held tensors (quant scales, MLA impl
carriers) are enumerated through the module graph and restored via
chained
installs with tuple sealing — no silently-skipped containers, dotted
dict
keys safe (`[{"a": ...}, {"i": ...}, {"k": ...}]` labeled access
chains).
- **Alias dedup**: tied weights are persisted once (`alias_of`,
nbytes=0) and
  re-share storage on restore.
- **Install-time validation**: schema v3 gate, per-run fingerprint
match, blob
  bounds checks, per-tensor spot hashes — tampering is caught even in
  size-only verify mode.
- **Fallback semantics**: a failed restore never kills startup — the
stale
snapshot is deleted, the instance falls back to a fresh load and
re-saves.

### 2. A shared weight-state enumeration kernel (`weight_state.py`)

"Which tensors constitute the final loaded weights, and where do they
live" is
the hard problem shared by all three weight-transfer loaders:

| loader | transfer plane | time span |
|---|---|---|
| bigtensorloader (H2D) | mmap + batched H2D | across restarts |
| netloader (D2D) | HCCL P2P stateless PG | live donor -> client |
| rfork (D2D) | YuanRong TransferEngine + planner/lease | live seed ->
receiver |

This PR centralizes enumeration into one module with **two documented
strategies** (they cannot be merged — their correctness definitions
differ):

- **Access-chain DFS** (`iter_module_weight_states`):
recovery-addressing
oriented — every tensor plus a labeled, JSON-serializable access chain
and
  container definitions; consumed by the snapshot manifest and netloader
  transfer items.
- **Canonical shortest-path BFS** (`collect_transferable_tensors`):
moved
**verbatim** from `rfork/tensor_layout.py` (upstream #17366) —
protocol-identity
oriented: deterministic per-rank canonical IDs for seed keys/manifests,
registered-first two-pass collection, ambiguity rejection; consumed by
rfork.
Tensor IDs / structural digests / seed keys are unchanged, covered by
336
  rfork UTs.

**Transfer lifecycles remain fully separate** (disk persistence vs HCCL
vs
TransferEngine+lease); only enumeration is shared. The transferability
predicates netloader had re-defined locally now import from the shared
module
(byte-identical logic).

Netloader also gains: pre-HCCL strong validation of tensor count/order
against
the donor manifest, and a dynamic-EPLB disable guard.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: new opt-in `--load-format bigtensorloader` with typed keys under
`--model-loader-extra-config` (`fast_restore`, `checkpoint_path`,
`verify`,
`bulk_h2d`, `bulk_chunk_mb`) - the same channel as netloader/rfork, with
no
new environment variables. No default
behavior changes; other loaders unaffected at runtime.

## How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests** (all green):
- rfork: 336 (incl. the moved BFS walker's canonical-ID, scan-dedup and
alias
behavior asserted bit-for-bit; the walker move required monkeypatch
homes to
  be re-pointed, documented in the conftest)
- netloader: 74 (incl. the new manifest-order validation and EPLB-guard
stubs)
- bigtensorloader: 35 on real NPU (snapshot v3 incl. NZ round-trips,
  truncation/tamper/fingerprint rejection, alias re-share, fallback)
- Note: 7 errors in `test_engram_local_loading.py` are a **pre-existing
  upstream issue** — the fixture stubs the engram package with an empty
`__path__` while `embedding.py` imports `.shared_pool`, which only
resolves
  via a session-level import side effect; reproduced identically on
  unmodified `main` in an import-isolated environment. Unrelated to this
  change.

**Real-NPU functional harness on the PR branch** (21/21): container
capture +
chained restore, alias re-share, truncated-blob rejection, spot-hash
tamper
detection in size-only mode, fingerprint mismatch handling,
fallback-on-corruption.

**Serving E2E — byte-identical outputs at temperature 0** (run on a
v0.18.0
backport of this stack, the serving-capable environment available for
local
validation; the PR branch itself is covered by the UTs + harness above
plus the
CI NPU gates):
- **H2D snapshot**, 5-model matrix (dense bf16 / dense / multimodal /
W8A8 /
  MoE+MLA): convert->restore 5/5, restore H2D 0.58–13.35s vs fresh-load
  readiness 70–181s, zero fallbacks.
- **H2D snapshot, larger models**: Qwen3-30B-A3B-W8A8 (TP1, 1732-tensor
manifest, 192 NZ chunks, 48 aliases): restore H2D 14.7s, ready 370s vs
fresh
441s. Qwen3-30B-A3B bf16 (TP2 full cycle): dual-rank save + restore,
fresh
  696s vs restore 401s, outputs identical 5/5.
- **netloader (HCCL P2P)**, 5-model matrix: donor->client 5/5, HCCL recv
1.45–2.74s for 339–1408 tensors, manifest count/order validation
exercised.
- **rfork (TransferEngine, RoCE host)**: Qwen3-30B-A3B-W8A8
seed->receiver:
29.16 GiB in 1.75s, outputs identical; TP2 coordination validated
end-to-end
  (seed fully up under TP2, planner lease lifecycle, dual-rank memory
  registration, rank0 transfer 28.46 GiB in 1.49s).
- To be covered by the CI NPU gate (`ready-precise`): the remaining TP>1
rfork transfer leg and dsv4-flash (requires a newer serving stack than
the
  local backport environment).

For A2/A3 SparseFlashMla CSA, repeated query rows and heads currently repeat scalar sparse-index and block-table address translation. This PR vectorizes the TopK-512 address calculation and caches the resulting physical KV addresses per AIV, reducing repeated address-translation work without changing attention arithmetic or the operator interface. ### Optimization eligibility The optimized path is selected only when **all** required conditions are met: - A2/A3 CSA with TND query layout and PA_BBND KV layout. - Query heads <= 64, one KV head, sparse block size = 1, and TopK = 512. - Compressed page size is a positive power of two. - Block-table row width <= 1024 entries. - The complete physical KV-pool element-offset range fits in int32. - The device is processing the supported complete TopK-512 slice and all sparse indices are valid; otherwise it falls back to the scalar path. [CI] Refuse to re-run E2E on a commit that already has a verdict (#22392)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`/run` used to start a brand-new full-matrix E2E run on every comment,
as long as no run was active. A commit that had already passed could be
re-queued for nothing, and a commit that had already failed was better
retried with `/rerun`, which only re-runs the failed jobs.

This PR makes `/run` start at most one gate run per commit:

| State of the head commit | `/run` behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| An E2E run is queued / in progress | no-op; reply points to `/rerun` |
| An E2E run is waiting for maintainer approval | no-op; reply explains
the approval |
| newest completed run **passed** | refuses; reply asks for a new commit
|
| newest completed run **finished without passing** | refuses; reply
points to `/rerun` |
| newest completed run was **cancelled**, or there is none | triggers
E2E as before |

The verdict is read from the **newest** completed `E2E` run on the head
SHA (`sort_by(.updated_at) | last`), not from "some run once passed", so
the answer stays correct when a finished run is restarted by hand from
the Actions page. `cancelled` is deliberately not a verdict: A lost
runner or a manual stop says nothing about the code, so such a commit
remains eligible for `/run`.

A refusal never touches the `ci-run` label, so no `labeled` event is
emitted and no E2E job is created. Both failure replies (runs lookup and
label re-arm) now link to the handler run log, so the requester can tell
a transient API error from a broken `PAT_TOKEN` without asking a
maintainer first.

Out of scope: automatically cancelling in-flight runs on a superseded
commit. That was drafted and deliberately dropped from this PR; it stays
a separate decision.

---

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, in the behaviour of the `/run` slash command: repeating `/run` on a
commit whose E2E has already settled is now refused instead of queuing
another run. No code, API or configuration surface changes.
`docs/source/community/slash-commands.md` is updated accordingly, and a
release note fragment is added.

---

### How was this patch tested?

Workflow-only change; `tests/ut` does not cover workflow YAML, so no
unit test was added. Verified locally before pushing:

- State machine exercised against 13 synthetic run lists (no runs;
single success / failure / timed_out / startup_failure / cancelled;
in-progress only; awaiting approval; pass-then-newer-failure;
failure-then-newer-success; success-then-newer-cancelled; active run
beating a completed pass; failures of other workflows ignored) – all
produced the expected `state`.
- 3 malformed API responses (`{"message": "Bad credentials"}`), missing
`workflow_runs`, non-JSON HTML) all fail closed: the lookup-failure
reply is posted, no `state` is emitted, nothing is triggered.
- `yaml.safe_load` and `bash -n` pass for the workflow and every inline
`run:` block.

[BugFix] Align dummy_inputs_embeds with the upstream input_ids API (#22530)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The paired vLLM revision (`c410543d`) calls
`dummy_inputs_embeds(num_tokens, input_ids)`, passing `None` when input
randomization is disabled. The Ascend override only accepts
`num_tokens`, causing a `TypeError` during MRV2 startup/profile for

compatibility with vLLM `v0.33.0`.

enabled/disabled embedding TP, multimodal/prompt-embedding buffers, and
