[CI][BugFix] Make the review-triggered ci-gate retrigger's no-CI-run outcome a green notice, and stamp the gate comment with freshness (#22574)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Two related CI/CD quality-of-signal fixes for the review-triggered
ci-gate retrigger (bot_ci_gate_refresh / bot_ci_gate_comment):

**1. The `no-ci` outcome no longer produces a red run.** When a
CODEOWNERS owner approves a commit that was pushed without `/run`, the
refresh bot has no E2E run to re-run the gate on. It exited 1, so the
Actions page showed a red ✗ "CI Gate Refresh" run whose entire content
was guidance ("comment `/run` to start E2E"). Maintainers read that red
X as "the CI is broken" — motivating example: run 44657341836 (PR
#21892).

The expected no-CI-run-yet flow is now a green notice:
`refresh_ci_gate.py` exits 0 with `::notice::`, signals the workflow via
`needs_comment`/`gate_verdict` step outputs, and the reason text still
reaches the PR through the comment bot under a neutral title ("...has no
CI run to re-run yet" instead of "...failed"). Real rerun API errors
(`rerun-error`) keep failing the job with the existing red contract —
only the expected flow changed.

**2. The ci-gate failure comment now carries a freshness stamp.** The
comment is updated in place instead of re-posted, so GitHub keeps it at
its original timeline position and readers could not tell whether it
describes the current head or a stale verdict from an older push. The
failure and resolved states now start with `Last updated: <UTC time> for
commit <sha>`. The timestamp is bumped on every judging run (including a
re-run of an unchanged failure), so an old timestamp reliably reads as
"the bot stopped working"; since in-place edits are silent on GitHub,
the bump costs no notifications.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No user-facing wheel/Docker behavior change. PR authors see: the
gate-failure comment now shows an update timestamp and commit; a
review-triggered retrigger with no CI run yet no longer shows a red
workflow run, only a neutral PR comment guiding to `/run`.

## How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests: `.github/workflows/scripts/test_refresh_ci_gate.py` —
updated the obsolete `test_no_ci_run_fails` (which asserted the
red-failure contract) and added two cases: no-run exits 0 with
`::notice::` + reason file, and no-run emits the step outputs the
workflow gates on. 30/30 pass.
- Body-building and timestamp-dedup logic of the comment bot
smoke-tested locally.
- `bash format.sh ci` passes.
- CI testing only beyond that: the workflow paths
(`bot_ci_gate_refresh.yaml`, `bot_ci_gate_comment.yaml`) only execute in
the repository context.

[Performance] Fuse Step5 residual add, RMSNorm, and BF16 cast (#22336)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Following up on #20946, fuse the Step5 decoder's residual add, RMSNorm
and BF16 activation conversion before and after attention on Ascend A5.
The Triton path is selected when FP32 residual mode is enabled and the
norm weight and residual are FP32. In the no-residual case the kernel
normalizes the FP32 activation and the wrapper reuses that activation as
the running residual.

Step5 is adapted for Ascend 950DT (A5). Validation for this
model-specific fused Triton kernel is limited to 950DT in FP32 residual
mode.

Pass the MoE FFN output to the next layer in its original dtype. The
fused kernel widens it on load and the fallback widens it when computing
the residual sum. The FP32 gate still receives its input through the
existing router path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No

### How was this patch tested?

#### Operator accuracy and performance

On one Ascend 950DT with CANN 9.3.0 and torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, all 14
operator tests passed. The fused output met the BF16 tolerance, and the
FP32 residual matched exactly.

The baseline runs `Cast(FP32) → torch_npu.npu_add_rms_norm →
Cast(BF16)`. Both paths used the same BF16 activations, FP32 residuals,
and equivalent norm weights, with the Step-5-Preview hidden size of 4096
and RMSNorm epsilon of `1e-5`. The baseline's effective norm scale was
precomputed. The table reports median NPU event time per call over 10

[CI][BugFix] Raise changed-docs link check deadline (#22547)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Docs link check workflow gives the changed-docs run a 300 s overall
deadline (`--timeout 300`). A docs change that touches a link-dense file
needs
more than that: in
[run 44517120007 / job
135535904283](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/44517120007/job/135535904283?pr=22004)
the job ran for 6m 7s and the checker stopped at its 300 s deadline.
Every URL
still in flight was reported as

unverified - overall check deadline exceeded before a result was
received

which is a blocking error, so the job failed with
`CI result: FAILED - 52 blocking error(s), 73 non-blocking warning(s)`
even
though many of those links were never actually checked.

This PR raises the changed-docs deadline to 1200 s, matching the
checker's
default (`Settings.total_timeout`) already used by the full scan in the
same
workflow. The job keeps `timeout-minutes: 30`, so a 20-minute checker
budget
still leaves room for checkout and dependency installation, and a slow
batch no
longer turns unchecked links into false failures.

The checker itself (`check_md_links.py`) is unchanged: links that are
actually
broken still fail the job, and the changed-docs path keeps its
`--files-from` scope instead of scanning the whole `docs/source` tree.
